newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel sees 2.5 bln Ffr 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel sees 2.5 bln Ffr 1996 profit.

text.p: France's largest industrial group, electrical engineering giant Alcatel Alsthom, said on Thursday it expected to show a net profit of some 2.5 billion francs ($451.7 million) for 1996 after suffering one of the worst French corporate losses the year before.

"After taking into account exceptional items, and in particular capital gains resulting from the non-strategic asset disposal programme, the group's 1996 net income should amount to approximately 2.5 billion (francs)," Alcatel said in a statement on its provisional earnings analysis for 1996.
Alcatel is provisionally scheduled to report 1996 earnings on March 18.

The statement said 1996 sales amounted to 162.0 billion francs, showing little change over 1995, and orders increased by eight percent to 168.2 billion francs, reflecting an improvement in business activity.
Last September Alcatel said it had cut its first-half loss to 400 million francs in 1996, from 1.2 billion in the first six months of 1995, and predicted a profit for 1996.
The company lost 25.6 billion francs in 1995 after heavy restructuring charges. ($ = 5.534 French Francs)
